chunks: And it has been narrated from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him:
"An obligatory salat (prayer) is better than twenty hajj pilgrimages, and one hajj is better than a house filled with gold that is given in charity from it until it is exhausted."

key_terms.خَيْرٌ: better, more virtuous and superior in reward or rank
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: salat (prayer), the prescribed act of worship mentioned here in its obligatory form
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: obligatory, indicating a divinely mandated duty
key_terms.يَفْنَى: is depleted or comes to an end

ai.seo_question: Why is an obligatory prayer better than many hajj pilgrimages and great amounts of charity in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the immense merit of an obligatory salat (prayer), placing it above repeated acts of hajj and immense material charity. It highlights the centrality of divinely mandated worship and shows that the value of acts of devotion is determined by their rank with Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.630 - It has been narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):
"An obligatory prayer (fardh) is better than twenty pilgrimages (Hajj), and one Hajj is better than a house filled with gold given in charity until it is depleted."
